help.intro: A text of about 200 words about renting a flat in Germany, the country with the most tenants in Europe: about half of all Germans rent, in Berlin more than eighty per cent. The text explains the words every newcomer meets in an advert (Kaltmiete, Warmmiete, Nebenkosten, Kaution, WG), why a German kitchen sometimes leaves with the old tenant, why you must register at the town hall within two weeks and why the quiet hours matter. All facts are real and were checked. You read what you have just learnt: weil and dass with the verb at the end (… weil die Miete hoch ist; Viele wissen nicht, dass die Küche fehlt), and wenn … (dann) and deshalb for conditions and consequences. Read for the gist first, then find one term or one rule per question.
help.tips[0].title: weil and dass: verb at the end
help.tips[0].text: weil (because) and dass (that) start a subordinate clause; the verb goes to the end: Viele Deutsche mieten, weil Häuser teuer sind. Man muss wissen, dass die Küche oft fehlt. With a modal verb, the modal is last: …, dass man sich anmelden muss. With the Perfekt, haben/sein is last: …, weil der Mieter die Küche mitgenommen hat. Comma before weil and dass.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Many Germans rent all their life because houses and flats are very expensive.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: New tenants are often surprised that the flat has no kitchen.
help.tips[0].check.q: Ich suche eine WG, weil ich nicht viel Geld ____.
help.tips[0].check.why: After weil the verb stands at the end of the clause: … weil ich nicht viel Geld habe.
help.tips[1].text: wenn (if, when) starts a subordinate clause with the verb at the end; the main clause can start with dann and puts its verb first: Wenn man umzieht, (dann) muss man sich anmelden. deshalb (that is why) gives the consequence and takes position 1 in a main clause, verb in position 2: Die Mieten sind hoch, deshalb wohnen viele in einer WG. Same meaning, two directions: weil gives the reason, deshalb the result.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: If you rent a flat, you usually have to pay three months' rent as deposit.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Flats in Berlin are expensive, that is why many young people live in a shared flat.
help.tips[1].check.q: Die Miete ist hoch, ____ suche ich eine kleinere Wohnung.
help.tips[1].check.why: The second clause is the consequence: deshalb (that is why) with the verb right after it.
help.remember[0]: weil / dass / wenn: verb at the end of the clause; deshalb: verb in position 2.
help.remember[1]: Kaltmiete + Nebenkosten = Warmmiete; Kaution = up to three months' rent; WG = shared flat.
help.exam: Short practical texts about housing with explanations of terms and multiple-choice questions are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: Cold rent, warm rent, three months' deposit and a kitchen that leaves with the old tenant: read how renting works in Germany.
help.vocab[7].example: Das Geld bekommt man zurück, wenn man auszieht.
passageTranslation:
In Germany about half the people live in a rented flat. That is more than in any other country in Europe. In Berlin it is even over eighty per cent. Many Germans rent all their life, because houses and flats are very expensive and because tenants have good rights.

Whoever looks for a flat must know a few words. The Kaltmiete, cold rent, is the price for the flat. Added to it are the Nebenkosten, extra costs: heating, water, rubbish, caretaker. Cold rent plus extra costs is the Warmmiete, warm rent. Electricity and internet you pay separately. And you must pay a Kaution, a deposit, usually three cold rents. You get the money back when you move out and the flat is in order.

A surprise for many foreigners: often the flat has no kitchen! The kitchen belongs to the old tenant, and he takes it with him. Sometimes you can buy it from him.

When you move, you must register at the citizens' office within two weeks. That is compulsory. Without the registration you get no bank account and no mobile contract.

Young people and students often live in a WG, a shared flat. Everyone has a room, and kitchen and bathroom are shared. That is cheaper, which is why the WG is very popular in big cities.

And one more rule: from 10 pm to 6 am it is night quiet, from 1 to 3 pm often midday quiet. Whoever is loud then gets a letter from the landlord.
questions[0].explanation: "In Deutschland wohnt etwa die Hälfte der Menschen in einer Mietwohnung … In Berlin sind es sogar über achtzig Prozent."
questions[0].questionTranslation: How many people in Germany live in a rented flat?
questions[0].optionsTranslation[1]: about half, in Berlin over eighty per cent
questions[0].optionsTranslation[2]: almost all, except the people in the countryside
questions[1].explanation: After weil the verb (sind) goes to the end of the clause.
questions[1].questionTranslation: 'Many Germans rent all their life because houses and flats are very expensive.' Where is the verb in the weil clause?
questions[2].explanation: "Kaltmiete plus Nebenkosten ist die Warmmiete. Strom und Internet bezahlt man extra."
questions[2].optionsTranslation[1]: cold rent plus extra costs like heating and water
questions[2].optionsTranslation[2]: the rent including electricity, internet and all other costs
questions[3].options[1]: drei Kaltmieten; wenn man auszieht und die Wohnung in Ordnung ist
questions[3].explanation: "… eine Kaution zahlen, meistens drei Kaltmieten. Das Geld bekommt man zurück, wenn man auszieht und die Wohnung in Ordnung ist."
questions[3].questionTranslation: How high is the deposit usually, and when do you get it back?
questions[3].optionsTranslation[0]: one month's rent; after a year
questions[3].optionsTranslation[1]: three cold rents; when you move out and the flat is in order
questions[3].optionsTranslation[2]: three warm rents; you never get it back
questions[4].options[1]: weil die Küche dem alten Mieter gehört und er sie mitnimmt
questions[4].explanation: "Die Küche gehört dem alten Mieter, und er nimmt sie mit. Manchmal kann man sie ihm abkaufen."
questions[4].questionTranslation: Why does the flat often have no kitchen?
questions[4].optionsTranslation[0]: because kitchens are forbidden in Germany
questions[4].optionsTranslation[1]: because the kitchen belongs to the old tenant and he takes it
questions[4].optionsTranslation[2]: because people do not cook in Germany
questions[4].optionsTranslation[3]: because the landlord sells it before the new tenant comes
questions[5].explanation: "Ohne die Anmeldung bekommt man kein Bankkonto und keinen Handyvertrag."
questions[5].questionTranslation: 'When you move, you must register at the citizens' office within two weeks.' What happens without registration?
questions[5].optionsTranslation[0]: You do not get the deposit back.
questions[5].optionsTranslation[1]: You get no bank account and no mobile contract.
questions[5].optionsTranslation[2]: You have to move out again immediately and pay the deposit.
questions[6].explanation: deshalb introduces the consequence (that is why); the reason is in the clause before (billiger).
questions[6].questionTranslation: 'That is cheaper, that is why the WG is very popular in big cities.' What does deshalb express?
questions[7].explanation: "Von 22 bis 6 Uhr ist Nachtruhe, von 13 bis 15 Uhr oft Mittagsruhe."
questions[3].options[2]: drei Warmmieten; man bekommt sie nie zurück
questions[4].options[0]: weil Küchen in Deutschland verboten sind
questions[4].options[2]: weil man in Deutschland nicht kocht
questions[4].options[3]: weil der Vermieter sie verkauft, bevor der neue Mieter kommt
